Use Nx = 400 uniform finite-volume cells on the spatial domain [a, b] = [-1, 1] with cell centers x_j = -1 + (j + 0.5)*dx for j = 0,...,Nx-1, and dx = (b - a) / Nx = 0.005.
Use CFL = 0.5 in the convective time-step constraint.
Set the final integration time to T = 0.5, and adjust the final time step so that the simulation ends exactly at T.
Use the physical parameters Gamma = 1.6666666666666667, eta = 0.1, and zeta = eta = 0.1 exactly as specified.
Apply periodic boundary conditions at x = -1 and x = 1 by wrapping cell indices (no duplicated endpoint beyond the periodic wrap).
Initialize smooth fields at t = 0 pointwise on the cell centers using rho(x, 0) = 1.0 + 0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x, 0) = 0.1*cos(pi*x), and p(x, 0) = 1.0 + 0.2*cos(pi*x), all evaluated at x_j.
Define the conserved variables U = [rho, m, E] with m = rho*v and total energy E = p/(Gamma - 1) + 0.5*rho*v^2, and evolve cell averages of U on the finite-volume grid.
Compute the pressure from the conserved state as p = (Gamma - 1) * (E - 0.5*m^2/rho), and enforce positivity by clipping rho and p to a floor of 1e-12 whenever they become non-positive.
Compute the convective flux F_conv(U) = [m, m^2/rho + p, (E + p)*v] with v = m/rho.
At each cell interface, compute the sound speed c = sqrt(Gamma*p/rho) on each side, form the Rusanov (local Lax-Friedrichs) wave speed a = max(|v_L| + c_L, |v_R| + c_R), and use F_hat = 0.5*(F_conv(U_L) + F_conv(U_R)) - 0.5*a*(U_R - U_L).
Approximate v_x at cell centers with a centered difference on cell-centered v, set sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x, and approximate sigma at cell interfaces by averaging the two neighboring cell-centered values of sigma.
Form the interface viscous flux F_visc = [0, -sigma, -v*sigma] using interface-averaged v and sigma, and use the total interface flux F_total = F_hat + F_visc for the semi-discrete update.
Integrate the semi-discrete finite-volume system in time with 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method).
Choose the time step each step as dt = min(CFL*dx / max_j(|v_j| + c_j), 0.5*dx^2 / max(zeta + 4/3*eta, 1e-30)), where CFL = 0.5 and the max over j is taken over all interior cell centers.
At t = T = 0.5, recover the primitive fields on the cell centers via v = m/rho and p = (Gamma - 1)*(E - 0.5*m^2/rho), again applying the 1e-12 positivity floor to rho and p as needed.
Save a single NPZ file named "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz" containing the 1D arrays x (length Nx), rho, v, p (each length Nx) and the scalar metadata Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, and CFL = 0.5.
Save a figure named "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png" showing line plots of rho(x, T), v(x, T), and p(x, T) versus x at the final time, as a 3-panel or 3 separate line plots.
Print the min and max of rho and p at the final time as a positivity diagnostic and the spatial mean of rho over the domain as a mass-conservation diagnostic.
